chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Salaries in the Syncopated Orchestra
summary: Briggs earned about $75 a week as lead trumpet, the lowest musicians $50, and Withers and Bechet roughly $80-100.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, let's get up to that.
I just want to take you back a little bit and try and get some detail on this.
So, Latimore turned around and booked the band for a lot of dough, and he was paying you just small amounts?
Yes.
Do you remember what kind of salary the guys were getting?
Yes, I was getting a very big salary.
You were playing lead, were you?
Yes.
Solo?
Yes.
Briggs
I was making about $75.00 a week.
That's pretty good money for then.
You're telling me. As far as the band was concerned, the lowest price was about $60.00, a week. $50.00. $60.00 and $50.00. The very lowest for a musician was $50.00.
Right.
I know one trombone player had $60.00. Mr. Withers, naturally he made about $85.00 or $100.00. He was worth it. He did two or three numbers, solos, you see.
Right.
So, Bechet --
He was getting a lot.
Bechet must have been getting around, between $80.00, $85.00, a week.
